content.title: Find My FHA Mortgage Rates | Current FHA Interest Rates
content.text: This mortgage structure may have more flexible terms for financing approval, but FHA mortgage rates are typically the same as a conventional mortgage. Much like some of the more popular conventional mortgages, FHA loan rates are fixed, meaning the agreed-upon interest rate at the close of the sale will remain unchanged throughout the loan’s amortization schedule.This certainty allows FHA loan borrowers to understand exactly how much they’ll need to contribute for their mortgage payments for up to three decades, eliminating any worry of unexpected hikes in the cost of repaying money.Even though FHA mortgage rates don’t differ much from conventional mortgages, qualified borrowers for FHA loans may have different financial backgrounds and their interest rate can be altered as a result.In addition to economic forces and recent market trends, your specific FHA mortgage rate will depend on other factors, such as your current savings, history of managing debts and mortgage insurance requirements.On a conventional mortgage, such as a 15-year fixed loan, lenders might have different expectations of their borrowers. Anyone applying for this type of home financing would have to contribute 20% of the home’s sales price for a down payment to avoid PMI requirements, in addition to a strong credit score and financial background. If you can’t meet these standards, your insurance rates could increase as a result.Just like conventional mortgages, your credit background will still factor heavily on what your lender considers an appropriate FHA mortgage rate.Credit score requirementsMost lenders will require a minimum credit score of 620 to approve a conventional mortgage. FHA loans, alternatively, could be issued to borrowers with a lower score.While FHA loans do have lower credit thresholds for prospective borrowers, a higher credit score will still lead to a more favorable purchasing agreement. A lower credit score, on the other hand, will increase the rate of interest on your mortgage.Lower down paymentAs housing prices continue to rise, borrowers paying off their student debt or auto loans might not have the financial bandwidth for a conventional mortgage. One of the biggest hurdles in securing a mortgage is saving enough money for a sizable down payment, which is why many hopeful borrowers apply for FHA loans.FHA loan applicants with a low credit score will face different FHA down payment requirements. Lower down payment requirements are another advantage of FHA loans, but the amount you save depends on the quality of your credit score.FHA loan applicants with a credit score of 620 or higher could qualify for down payment options starting at 3.5%. Any lower than that, in the 500-610 range, usually means the borrower could qualify for down payment options starting at 10%, according to Investopedia.In addition to FHA mortgage rates, the amount you will pay for the down payment is heavily impacted by your credit score. Borrowers who are able to contribute more towards their FHA loan down payment typically get a lower interest rate as a result.
